Colophon

What's a colophon you ask? I'm glad you asked, because I also just recently learned what it is myself! I'll let Wikipedia explain it.

This site is built entirely from scratch, using basic HTML, extremely minimal CSS, and vim. That's it. Nothing special here. It's currently hosted on a Linode VPS. For the backing software, it's just Nginx and Let's Encrypt for certificate for HTTPS functionality.

For managing the source code, I'm hosting it on sourcehut. It's a very minimal interface for a reasonable price. I know I'm just scratching the surface of its featureset but it's been nice using software that's purpose-built for a given need, even if it does cost money. Better that than being the product.

I also don't use any minification tools to try to squeeze a little bit more compression out of these files. Modern gzip is already incredibly efficient at compressing text-based content, and once I get around to enabling brotli on this server, it'll be even smaller already. Feel free to poke around the source code using View Source in your browser! Fair warning - I'm not a developer by profession, this is purely a hobby. I try to get better at it every day, that's all that matters to me.

Unraid Server

I've been using Unraid for a few years now and it's honestly been incredible. I love how simple it is to build your own little ecosystem. It's easy to go overboard but with proper planning of share setups and container installs, it's fairly straightforward.

The items below is a list of the primary containers that I run:

  • changedetection.io & Browserless
    • These two I use for website update notifications. Mostly work related to track things that I can't subscribe to over email easily.
  • Mealie
    • Meal planner and recipe storage
  • Paperless-ngx
  • Pihole
  • freshrss
  • Nextcloud
  • Nginx Proxy Manager

Most of my servers are available on my local network through Nginx Proxy Manager by hostname with valid TLS certificate through Let's Encrypt. I don't expose any services to the public internet from home, however, I do run a Wireguard VPN on my Unifi Cloud Gateway Ultra that allows me to access it as if I were home. It also has an added benefit of off-network adblocking thanks to the Pihole setup.
